newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN CONDEMNS ISRAELI TUNNEL, SETTLEMENT TORTURE.
newsitem.headline: UN CONDEMNS ISRAELI TUNNEL, SETTLEMENT TORTURE.

text.p: The U.N. Human Rights Commission on Wednesday condemned alleged abuses by Israel in occupied Arab territories, including torture of Palestinians, settlement in Arab East Jerusalem and the opening of an ancient tunnel which offended Moslems.

The United States, a close ally of Israel, was alone in voting against four of the five resolutions on the Middle East which were adopted by the 53-member body. The Jewish state is an observer at the annual six-week session in Geneva.
The fifth -- a U.S.-sponsored motion backing the peace process and calling for continued negotiations on implementing the next stage -- was adopted without a vote.

One motion, sponsored by more than 20 European states including Britain, France, Germany and overwhelmingly adopted, urged Israel to halt its settlement expansion policy in the occupied territories, calling it a "major obstacle to peace".
The Commission, pushed by Arab states, examines Israeli practices in the occupied territories as a separate item on its agenda -- a ritual which Israel denounces as discriminatory.
As voting took place, the United States ordered its chief Middle East peace broker Dennis Roth back to the region, where violence flared for a seventh straight day.

The most strongly-worded resolution, on violation of human rights in the occupied Arab territories, including Palestine, was put forward by 16 states including Algeria, Bahrain, Bangladesh, China, Cuba, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Malaysia, Morocco, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Tunisia and Yemen.
It was adopted by a vote of 25 states in favour, one against (the United States), with 24 abstentions and three states absent during the vote, according to an official U.N. tally.

The text condemns Israel for continued violations of human rights -- and demands it cease them immediately -- "in particular the continuation of acts of killing, the detention of thousands of Palestinians without trial, the continuation of the confiscation of lands, the extension and the establishment of Israeli settlements, the confiscation of property of Palestinians and expropriation of their land".

The commission said it "also condemns the opening of a tunnel under the Al Aqsa mosque, the establishment of an Israeli settlement on Jabal Abu Ghenaim in occupied Arab Jerusalem, the revocation of identity cards of the citizens of the Palestinian city of Jerusalem and forcing them to live outside their home with the aim of the Judaization of Jerusalem, and calls upon the Government of Israel to close the tunnel and to immediately put an end to these practices".

Israeli leaders angrily deny that the tunnel passes beneath or undermines al-Aqsa mosque. When archaeologists opened a second entrance in September 1996, so that visitors could follow the tunnel from end to end, the dispute touched off riots in which 61 Palestinians and 15 Israelis died.
The resolution also denounced "the use of torture against Palestinians during interrogation, which the Israeli High Court of Justice has legitimised".
The text called upon Israel to cease "its policy of enforcing collective punishments", such as demolition of houses and closure of the Palestinian territory.

A separate resolution, adopted by a vote of 28 states in favour, one against, with 21 abstentions and three states absent, backed self-determination and called on Israel to withdraw from the Palestinian territories, including Jerusalem.

A resolution on Israeli settlements in the occupied Arab territories, sponsored by European countries and Australia and Japan, expressed "deep concern" at the Israeli settlement activities, including land expropriation, and called for a halt.

"...since they are illegal, (the activities) constitute a violation of the Geneva Convention relative to the protection of civilian persons in time of war, of 12 August 1949 and are a major obstacle to peace," it said. The text was adopted by a vote of 47 states in favour, one against, with two abstentions and three states absent.
A motion on the Golan Heights, which Israel captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East War, was sponsored by 19 states including Syria.
It urged Israel to end its occupation and rescind 1981 laws "which has resulted in the effective annexation of that territory".
A resolution on the Middle East peace process, sponsored by 13 states including the United States, welcomed progress since Madrid talks in 1991.

It encouraged continuation of negotiations on implementing the next stage of the Declaration of Principles on Interim Self-Government Arrangements, signed in September 1993 by Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
